answer: Give every identity a work quota that starts at zero and grows only from completed, peer-verified jobs, so a fresh identity is hollow: it can do nothing until it has done real work. A sybil farm must therefore pay the full labour cost of each puppet history before any of them earns, and the quota decays if the identity goes idle, so stockpiled puppets rot. The fable that one key equals one voice dies here: at the zenith of influence sit only identities with long, checkable work trails, and forging one costs more than the payout it unlocks.
